results.title: Tesla launches FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes | Electrek
results.content:
> v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:
> 
> Upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, which is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency, improving the critical intervention rate by 25x.
> 
> Introduced Tesla Augmented Reality, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.
> 
> Improved navigation by using an end-to-end learned model based on route preference data from the fleet.
> 
> Improved parking location selection by using personalized parking history, and the map will now display multiple parking options at your destination.
> [...] Tesla calls it “Reality View” in its announcement and “Tesla Augmented Reality” in the release notes. The notes say it replaces all the separate model signals with a single end-to-end visualization that uses less compute, and Tesla says it lets the driver “see & control what FSD is planning to do.” If that works as advertised, it could make supervising the system a lot easier.

## v15 goes after FSD’s biggest weak spots

What stands out more is where Tesla is focusing. Almost every driving improvement in the release notes targets an area where FSD struggles today. [...] Tesla has started rolling out “Full Self-Driving” v15, and its list of improvements reads like a list of FSD’s biggest current weaknesses: sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones.

Tesla also claims “25x better handling of safety critical cases” and is adding a new live visualization that looks seriously impressive. If the driving improvements are as real as the visuals, this is a big update.

## What’s in FSD v15

Tesla announced the rollout on X this afternoon, and its Tesla Super Intelligence account followed up with the full release notes. The company didn’t say which vehicles get it first, but it has previously told investors that its AI4 (HW4) computer is enough to run v15.

Here are Tesla’s release notes for FSD v15:

The UI changes will likely upgrade AMD Ryzen-equipped Tesla vehicles running AI4 to visualize vehicles using the Unreal Engine, something that was found in coding last year:

> Tesla plans to use Unreal Engine for driver visualization with crazy upgrade

Additionally, one user stated that their biggest complaints with v14’s most recent releases is that they have to “stop refusing to use the HOV lane” and last-second lane changes to merge or turn happen too frequently. Musk said these should be fixed in v15.

results.title: Tom Adda on Facebook: "# **FSD V15 is far more than just a visual upgrade.** # **V15 Release Notes:** –V15 upgrades every p…"
results.content:
# Tom Adda on Facebook: "# FSD V15 is far more than just a visual upgrade. # V15 Release Notes: –V15 upgrades every p…"

# FSD V15 is far more than just a visual upgrade.

# V15 Release Notes:

–V15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network.

–Upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, which is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency, improving the critical intervention rate by 25x.

–Introduced Tesla Reality View, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.

–Improved navigation by using an end-to-end learned model based on route preference data from the fleet. [...] –Ability to toggle between full screen Reality View and also a "full screen" basic NAV map view.

-Disengagement menu removed

–Improved parking location selection by using personalized parking history, and the map will now display multiple parking options at your destination.

–Improved driver monitoring by increasing vision-based attention monitoring availability with hats and sunglasses and decreasing strictness in higher speed driver profiles.

–Improved detection of road signs, small animals, road debris, and chains.

–Improved detection of potholes, road details, and avoidance of deep standing water.

–Improved speed handling for each driver profile, school zones and speed limits, and inclement weather. [...] –Improved Autoshift functionality by unifying with FSD-based gear predictions.

results.title: Tesla FSD V15 Offers Stunning Visualizations That Distract From “25x”
results.content:
The visualization is cool, and a real achievement, but it does not affect the driving performance of the system, and in fact you should not have something distracting on the screen when your eyes are supposed to be on the road. Far more interesting is the second line in their release notes:

> v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:

> - Upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, which is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency, improving the critical intervention rate by 25x.

> - Introduced Tesla Reality View, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.
